statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: each end of the PPP link MUST first send LCP packets to configure and test the data link
actions: send LCP packets to configure and test data link

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: After the link has been established, the peer MAY be authenticated

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: PPP MUST send NCP packets to choose and configure one or more network-layer protocols
actions: send NCP packets to choose and configure network-layer protocols

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Once each of the chosen network-layer protocols has been configured, datagrams from each network-layer protocol can be sent over the link

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The link will remain configured for communications until explicit LCP or NCP packets close the link down
statements.trigger: explicit LCP or NCP close packets

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The link will remain configured for communications until some external event occurs (an inactivity timer expires)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The link will remain configured for communications until some external event occurs (network administrator intervention)

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: Dead phase: the starting and ending phase of the PPP link; the link is not active.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: Establish phase: the PPP link is being configured.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: Authenticate phase: the PPP link is undergoing authentication.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: Network phase: the PPP link is established and carrying network traffic.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: Terminate phase: the PPP link is being torn down.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: When the link layer signals UP, the PPP link moves from Dead to Establish.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: When the Establish phase succeeds (OPENED), the PPP link moves to Authenticate.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: When the Establish phase fails (FAIL), the PPP link returns to Dead.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: When authentication succeeds or is not required (SUCCESS/NONE), the PPP link moves from Authenticate to Network.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: When authentication fails (FAIL), the PPP link moves from Authenticate to Terminate.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: When the network layer closes (CLOSING), the PPP link moves from Network to Terminate.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: When the link layer signals DOWN, the PPP link moves from Terminate to Dead.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The link necessarily begins and ends with this phase.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: During this phase, the LCP automaton will be in the Initial or Starting states.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: During this phase, the LCP automaton will be in the Initial or Starting states.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When an external event (such as carrier detection or network administrator configuration) indicates that the physical-layer is ready to be used, PPP will proceed to the Link Establishment phase.
statements.trigger: physical-layer ready (carrier detection or network administrator configuration)
actions: signal Up event to LCP automaton

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The transition to the Link Establishment phase will signal an Up event to the LCP automaton.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Link Control Protocol (LCP) is used to establish the connection through an exchange of Configure packets.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: This exchange is complete, and the LCP Opened state entered, once a Configure-Ack packet has been both sent and received.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: This exchange is complete, and the LCP Opened state entered, once a Configure-Ack packet has been both sent and received.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Any non-LCP packets received during this phase MUST be silently discarded.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The receipt of the LCP Configure-Request causes a return to the Link Establishment phase from the Network-Layer Protocol phase.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The receipt of the LCP Configure-Request causes a return to the Link Establishment phase from the Authentication phase.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Authentication Phase - a phase during which a peer may be required to authenticate itself before allowing network-layer protocol packets to be exchanged.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Authentication SHOULD take place as soon as possible after link establishment.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Advancement from the Authentication phase to the Network-Layer Protocol phase MUST NOT occur until authentication has completed.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If authentication fails, the authenticator SHOULD proceed instead to the Link Termination phase.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: All other packets received during this phase MUST be silently discarded.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The authentication SHOULD allow some method of retransmission, and proceed to the Link Termination phase only after a number of authentication attempts has been exceeded.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: Once PPP has finished the previous phases, each network-layer protocol MUST be separately configured by the appropriate Network Control Protocol (NCP).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After a NCP has reached the Opened state, PPP will carry the corresponding network-layer protocol packets.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Each NCP MAY be Opened and Closed at any time.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After a NCP has reached the Opened state, PPP will carry the corresponding network-layer protocol packets.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Any supported network-layer protocol packets received when the corresponding NCP is not in the Opened state MUST be silently discarded.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: While LCP is in the Opened state, any protocol packet which is unsupported by the implementation MUST be returned in a Protocol-Reject.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: LCP is used to close the link through an exchange of Terminate packets. When the link is closing, PPP informs the network-layer protocols so that they may take appropriate action.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: PPP SHOULD proceed to the Link Dead phase after the exchange of Terminate packets.

statements.subject: ppp
statements.description: PPP can terminate the link at any time. This might happen because of the loss of carrier, authentication failure, link quality failure, the expiration of an idle-period timer, or the administrative closing of the link.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The sender of the Terminate-Request SHOULD disconnect after receiving a Terminate-Ack. PPP SHOULD proceed to the Link Dead phase.
statements.pre_cond: endpoint.role = Terminate-Request-sender & protocol.state = Link Termination Phase

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The sender of the Terminate-Request SHOULD disconnect after the Restart counter expires. PPP SHOULD proceed to the Link Dead phase.
statements.pre_cond: endpoint.role = Terminate-Request-sender & protocol.state = Link Termination Phase

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The receiver of a Terminate-Request SHOULD wait for the peer to disconnect, and MUST NOT disconnect until at least one Restart time has passed after sending a Terminate-Ack.
statements.pre_cond: endpoint.role = Terminate-Request-receiver & protocol.state = Link Termination Phase & timer.restart_time_elapsed = true

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Any non-LCP packets received during this phase MUST be silently discarded.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The sender of the Terminate-Request SHOULD disconnect after receiving a Terminate-Ack, or after the Restart counter expires.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The finite-state automaton is defined by events, actions and state transitions. Events include reception of external commands such as Open and Close, expiration of the Restart timer, and reception of packets from a peer. Actions include the starting of the Restart timer and transmission of packets to the peer.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the Initial state, the lower layer is unavailable (Down), and no Open has occurred. The Restart timer is not running in the Initial state.
statements.invariant_cond: lower_layer.state = Down & open.occurred = false & restart_timer.running = false

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Starting state is the Open counterpart to the Initial state. An administrative Open has been initiated, but the lower layer is still unavailable (Down). The Restart timer is not running in the Starting state.
statements.invariant_cond: open.initiated = true & lower_layer.state = Down & restart_timer.running = false

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the Closed state, the link is available (Up), but no Open has occurred. The Restart timer is not running in the Closed state.
statements.invariant_cond: lower_layer.state = Up & open.occurred = false & restart_timer.running = false

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Stopped state is the Open counterpart to the Closed state. It is entered when the automaton is waiting for a Down event after the This-Layer-Finished action, or after sending a Terminate-Ack. The Restart timer is not running in the Stopped state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the Closing state, an attempt is made to terminate the connection. A Terminate-Request has been sent and the Restart timer is running, but a Terminate-Ack has not yet been received.
statements.invariant_cond: terminate_request.sent = true & restart_timer.running = true & terminate_ack.received = false

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Stopping state is the Open counterpart to the Closing state. A Terminate-Request has been sent and the Restart timer is running, but a Terminate-Ack has not yet been received.
statements.invariant_cond: terminate_request.sent = true & restart_timer.running = true & terminate_ack.received = false

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the Request-Sent state an attempt is made to configure the connection. A Configure-Request has been sent and the Restart timer is running, but a Configure-Ack has not yet been received nor has one been sent.
statements.invariant_cond: configure_request.sent = true & restart_timer.running = true & configure_ack.received = false & configure_ack.sent = false

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the Ack-Received state, a Configure-Request has been sent and a Configure-Ack has been received. The Restart timer is still running, since a Configure-Ack has not yet been sent.
statements.invariant_cond: configure_request.sent = true & configure_ack.received = true & configure_ack.sent = false & restart_timer.running = true

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the Ack-Sent state, a Configure-Request and a Configure-Ack have both been sent, but a Configure-Ack has not yet been received. The Restart timer is running, since a Configure-Ack has not yet been received.
statements.invariant_cond: configure_request.sent = true & configure_ack.sent = true & configure_ack.received = false & restart_timer.running = true

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the Opened state, a Configure-Ack has been both sent and received. The Restart timer is not running.
statements.invariant_cond: configure_ack.sent = true & configure_ack.received = true & restart_timer.running = false

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When the lower layer becomes available (Up), a Configure-Request is sent.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Upon reception of Configure-Request packets, a Terminate-Ack is sent. Terminate-Acks are silently discarded to avoid creating a loop.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Terminate-Acks are silently discarded to avoid creating a loop. (in Closed state)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Upon reception of Configure-Request packets, an appropriate response is sent. (in Stopped state)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Upon reception of other packets, a Terminate-Ack is sent. (in Stopped state)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Terminate-Acks are silently discarded to avoid creating a loop. (in Stopped state)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Down event will supercede by returning the automaton to the Starting state. (from Stopped, when a Configure-Request arrives before the Down event)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Upon reception of a Terminate-Ack, the Closed state is entered. (from Closing)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Upon the expiration of the Restart timer, a new Terminate-Request is transmitted, and the Restart timer is restarted. (TO+ in Closing)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: After the Restart timer has expired Max-Terminate times, the Closed state is entered. (TO- in Closing)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When entering the Opened state, the implementation SHOULD signal the upper layers that it is now Up.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Conversely, when leaving the Opened state, the implementation SHOULD signal the upper layers that it is now Down.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The Restart timer is running in Closing and Stopping states (Terminate-Request sent, Terminate-Ack not yet received); not running in Initial, Starting, Closed, Stopped, and Opened states.
statements.guard_semantics: restart_timer.running = true iff connection.state = Closing | connection.state = Stopping | connection.state = Request-Sent | connection.state = Ack-Received | connection.state = Ack-Sent

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The Up event occurs when a lower layer indicates that it is ready to carry packets, signaling LCP that the link is entering Link Establishment phase.
actions: signal LCP that link is entering Link Establishment phase

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The This-Layer-Up action from LCP triggers the Up event in the NCP.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The Down event occurs when a lower layer indicates that it is no longer ready to carry packets, signaling LCP that the link is entering Link Dead phase.
actions: signal LCP that link is entering Link Dead phase

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The This-Layer-Down action from LCP triggers the Down event in the NCP.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: When the Open event occurs, and the link is not in the Opened state, the automaton attempts to send configuration packets to the peer.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: When an Open user command is executed in the Opened, Closing, Stopping, or Stopped states, the implementation should issue a Down event, immediately followed by an Up event.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Opened | protocol.state = Closing | protocol.state = Stopping | protocol.state = Stopped

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The Down followed by an Up will cause an orderly renegotiation of the link, by progressing through the Starting to the Request-Sent state.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: When the Close event occurs, and the link is not in the Closed state, the automaton attempts to terminate the connection. Further attempts to re-configure the link are denied until a new Open event occurs.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The Close followed by an Open will cause an orderly termination of the link, by progressing through the Closing to the Stopping state, and the This-Layer-Finished action can disconnect the link. The automaton waits in the Stopped or Starting states for the next connection attempt.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The TO+ event indicates that the Restart counter continues to be greater than zero, which triggers the corresponding Configure-Request or Terminate-Request packet to be retransmitted.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The TO- event indicates that the Restart counter is not greater than zero, and no more packets need to be retransmitted.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The Restart timer is used to time responses to Configure-Request and Terminate-Request packets. The TO+/TO- discrimination depends on the Restart counter value.
statements.guard_semantics: restart_counter > 0 selects TO+; restart_counter = 0 selects TO-

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RCR+ event indicates that the Configure-Request was acceptable, and triggers the transmission of a corresponding Configure-Ack.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RCR- event indicates that the Configure-Request was unacceptable, and triggers the transmission of a corresponding Configure-Nak or Configure-Reject.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: RCR+ and RCR- events may occur on a connection which is already in the Opened state. The implementation MUST be prepared to immediately renegotiate the Configuration Options.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: RCR+ and RCR- events may occur on a connection which is already in the Opened state. The implementation MUST be prepared to immediately renegotiate the Configuration Options.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RCA event occurs when a valid Configure-Ack packet is received from the peer. An out of sequence or otherwise invalid packet is silently discarded.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RCN event occurs when a valid Configure-Nak or Configure-Reject packet is received from the peer. An out of sequence or otherwise invalid packet is silently discarded.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RTR event occurs when a Terminate-Request packet is received. The implementation MUST be prepared to receive a new Configure-Request without network administrator intervention.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RTA event occurs when a Terminate-Ack packet is received from the peer. The Terminate-Ack packet may also indicate that the peer is in Closed or Stopped states, and serves to re-synchronize the link configuration.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RUC event occurs when an un-interpretable packet is received from the peer. A Code-Reject packet is sent in response.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RXJ+ event arises when the rejected value is acceptable, such as a Code-Reject of an extended code, or a Protocol-Reject of a NCP. These are within the scope of normal operation. The implementation MUST stop sending the offending packet type.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RXJ- event arises when the rejected value is catastrophic, such as a Code-Reject of Configure-Request, or a Protocol-Reject of LCP. This event communicates an unrecoverable error that terminates the connection.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The RXR event occurs when an Echo-Request, Echo-Reply or Discard-Request packet is received from the peer. There is no reply to an Echo-Reply or Discard-Request packet.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This action indicates to the upper layers that the automaton is entering the Opened state.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This action indicates to the lower layers that the automaton is entering the Starting state, and the lower layer is needed for the link.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This action indicates to the lower layers that the automaton is entering the Initial, Closed or Stopped states, and the lower layer is no longer needed for the link.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This action indicates to the lower layers that the automaton is entering the Initial, Closed or Stopped states, and the lower layer is no longer needed for the link.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This action indicates to the lower layers that the automaton is entering the Initial, Closed or Stopped states, and the lower layer is no longer needed for the link.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The Restart timer is started when the Configure-Request packet is transmitted, to guard against packet loss. The Restart timer is started when the Terminate-Request packet is transmitted, to guard against packet loss.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This action sets the Restart counter to the appropriate value (Max-Terminate or Max-Configure). The counter is decremented for each transmission, including the first.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Illegal-Event (-): This indicates an event that cannot occur in a properly implemented automaton. The implementation has an internal error, which should be reported and logged. No transition is taken, and the implementation SHOULD NOT reset or freeze.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This-Layer-Up (tlu): This action indicates to the upper layers that the automaton is entering the Opened state.
actions: signal Up event to upper layer

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This-Layer-Down (tld): This action indicates to the upper layers that the automaton is leaving the Opened state.
actions: signal Down event to upper layer

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This-Layer-Started (tls): This action indicates to the lower layers that the automaton is entering the Starting state, and the lower layer is needed for the link. The lower layer SHOULD respond with an Up event when the lower layer is available.
actions: lower layer responds with Up event when available

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This-Layer-Finished (tlf): This action indicates to the lower layers that the automaton is entering the Initial, Closed or Stopped states, and the lower layer is no longer needed for the link. The lower layer SHOULD respond with a Down event when the lower layer has terminated.
actions: signal lower layer no longer needed
lower layer responds with Down event when terminated

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This-Layer-Finished (tlf): This action indicates to the lower layers that the automaton is entering the Initial, Closed or Stopped states, and the lower layer is no longer needed for the link.
actions: signal lower layer no longer needed
lower layer responds with Down event when terminated

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: This-Layer-Finished (tlf): This action indicates to the lower layers that the automaton is entering the Initial, Closed or Stopped states, and the lower layer is no longer needed for the link.
actions: signal lower layer no longer needed
lower layer responds with Down event when terminated

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Initialize-Restart-Count (irc): This action sets the Restart counter to the appropriate value (Max-Terminate or Max-Configure). The counter is decremented for each transmission, including the first. The implementation MUST set the timeout period to the initial value when Restart timer backoff is used.
actions: set Restart counter to Max-Terminate or Max-Configure
set timeout period to initial value

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Zero-Restart-Count (zrc): This action sets the Restart counter to zero. This action enables the FSA to pause before proceeding to the desired final state, allowing traffic to be processed by the peer. The implementation MUST set the timeout period to an appropriate value.
actions: set timeout period to appropriate value

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Send-Configure-Request (scr): A Configure-Request packet is transmitted. The Restart timer is started when the Configure-Request packet is transmitted, to guard against packet loss. The Restart counter is decremented each time a Configure-Request is sent.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Send-Configure-Ack (sca): A Configure-Ack packet is transmitted. This acknowledges the reception of a Configure-Request packet with an acceptable set of Configuration Options.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Send-Configure-Nak (scn): A Configure-Nak or Configure-Reject packet is transmitted, as appropriate. This negative response reports the reception of a Configure-Request packet with an unacceptable set of Configuration Options.
actions: transmit Configure-Nak packet or Configure-Reject packet

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Send-Terminate-Request (str): A Terminate-Request packet is transmitted. The Restart timer is started when the Terminate-Request packet is transmitted, to guard against packet loss. The Restart counter is decremented each time a Terminate-Request is sent.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Send-Terminate-Ack (sta): A Terminate-Ack packet is transmitted. This acknowledges the reception of a Terminate-Request packet or otherwise serves to synchronize the automatons.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Send-Code-Reject (scj): A Code-Reject packet is transmitted. This indicates the reception of an unknown type of packet.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Send-Echo-Reply (ser): An Echo-Reply packet is transmitted. This acknowledges the reception of an Echo-Request packet.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Expiration of the Restart timer causes a Timeout event, and retransmission of the corresponding Configure-Request or Terminate-Request packet.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Max-Terminate indicates the number of Terminate-Request packets sent without receiving a Terminate-Ack before assuming that the peer is unable to respond. Max-Terminate MUST be configurable, but SHOULD default to two (2) transmissions.
statements.guard_semantics: Guards transition when Terminate-Request count exhausted without Terminate-Ack received

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Max-Configure indicates the number of Configure-Request packets sent without receiving a valid Configure-Ack, Configure-Nak or Configure-Reject before assuming that the peer is unable to respond. Max-Configure MUST be configurable, but SHOULD default to ten (10) transmissions.
statements.guard_semantics: Guards transition when Configure-Request count exhausted without valid Configure-Ack, Configure-Nak, or Configure-Reject received

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Max-Failure indicates the number of Configure-Nak packets sent without sending a Configure-Ack before assuming that configuration is not converging. Any further Configure-Nak packets for peer requested options are converted to Configure-Reject packets, and locally desired options are no longer appended. Max-Failure MUST be configurable, but SHOULD default to five (5) transmissions.
statements.guard_semantics: When exceeded, Convert Configure-Nak to Configure-Reject and suppress locally desired options

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: When a packet is received with an unknown Code field, a Code-Reject packet is transmitted.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: When a packet is received with an invalid Identifier field, the packet is silently discarded without affecting the automaton.
statements.guard_semantics: invalid Identifier => silent discard, automaton.state unchanged

statements.subject: message
statements.description: When a packet is received with an invalid Length field, the packet is silently discarded without affecting the automaton.
statements.guard_semantics: invalid Length => silent discard, automaton.state unchanged

statements.subject: message
statements.description: There are three classes of LCP packets: Link Configuration packets (Configure-Request, Configure-Ack, Configure-Nak, Configure-Reject), Link Termination packets (Terminate-Request, Terminate-Ack), and Link Maintenance packets (Code-Reject, Protocol-Reject, Echo-Request, Echo-Reply, Discard-Request).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An implementation wishing to open a connection MUST transmit a Configure-Request.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Upon reception of a Configure-Request, an appropriate reply MUST be transmitted.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Identifier field MUST be changed whenever the contents of the Options field changes, and whenever a valid reply has been received for a previous request. For retransmissions, the Identifier MAY remain unchanged.
statements.guard_semantics: must change when Options change or valid reply received; may remain unchanged for retransmissions

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If every Configuration Option received in a Configure-Request is recognizable and all values are acceptable, then the implementation MUST transmit a Configure-Ack.
actions: transmit Configure-Ack with acknowledged options unmodified and in original order

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On reception of a Configure-Ack, the Identifier field MUST match that of the last transmitted Configure-Request. Additionally, the Configuration Options in a Configure-Ack MUST exactly match those of the last transmitted Configure-Request.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Invalid packets are silently discarded.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: On reception of a Configure-Ack, the Identifier field MUST match that of the last transmitted Configure-Request.
statements.allowed_values: value equal to last transmitted Configure-Request Identifier

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Configuration Options in a Configure-Ack MUST exactly match those of the last transmitted Configure-Request.
statements.allowed_values: exact copy of Options from last transmitted Configure-Request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: On reception of a Configure-Nak, the Identifier field MUST match that of the last transmitted Configure-Request. Invalid packets are silently discarded.
statements.allowed_values: must equal Identifier of last transmitted Configure-Request

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On reception of a Configure-Nak, the Identifier field MUST match that of the last transmitted Configure-Request. Invalid packets are silently discarded.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Reception of a valid Configure-Nak indicates that when a new Configure-Request is sent, the Configuration Options MAY be modified as specified in the Configure-Nak.
statements.post_cond: Configure-Request.Options may be modified per Configure-Nak
actions: update Configuration Options per Configure-Nak values

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If some Configuration Options received in a Configure-Request are not recognizable or are not acceptable for negotiation, then the implementation MUST transmit a Configure-Reject.
statements.trigger: Receive-Configure-Request with unrecognizable or unacceptable options
actions: Transmit Configure-Reject containing only the unacceptable Configuration Options from the Configure-Request

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On reception of a Configure-Reject, the Identifier field MUST match that of the last transmitted Configure-Request. Additionally, the Configuration Options in a Configure-Reject MUST be a proper subset of those in the last transmitted Configure-Request. Invalid packets are silently discarded.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Reception of a valid Configure-Reject indicates that when a new Configure-Request is sent, it MUST NOT include any of the Configuration Options listed in the Configure-Reject.
actions: Exclude all Configure-Reject listed options from next Configure-Request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: On reception of a Configure-Reject, the Identifier field MUST match that of the last transmitted Configure-Request.
statements.guard_semantics: Validity guard for Configure-Reject reception; mismatch causes silent discard

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Configuration Options in a Configure-Reject MUST be a proper subset of those in the last transmitted Configure-Request.
statements.guard_semantics: Validity guard for Configure-Reject reception; violation causes silent discard

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Reception of an unelicited Terminate-Ack indicates that the peer is in the Closed or Stopped states, or is otherwise in need of re-negotiation.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Reception of an unelicited Terminate-Ack indicates that the peer is in the Closed or Stopped states, or is otherwise in need of re-negotiation.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An implementation wishing to close a connection SHOULD transmit a Terminate-Request. Terminate-Request packets SHOULD continue to be sent until Terminate-Ack is received, the lower layer indicates that it has gone down, or a sufficiently large number have been transmitted such that the peer is down with reasonable certainty.
statements.post_cond: message.type = Terminate-Request & (message.Terminate-Ack_received = true | lower_layer.down = true | retransmit_limit_reached = true)
actions: retransmit Terminate-Request until Terminate-Ack received or lower layer goes down or retransmit limit reached

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Upon reception of a Terminate-Request, a Terminate-Ack MUST be transmitted.
actions: copy Identifier from Terminate-Request into Terminate-Ack

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: Reception of an unelicited Terminate-Ack indicates that the peer is in the Closed or Stopped states, or is otherwise in need of re-negotiation.
statements.post_cond: peer.state = Closed | peer.state = Stopped | peer.needs_renegotiation = true
actions: infer peer state is Closed or Stopped

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Reception of a LCP packet with an unknown Code indicates that the peer is operating with a different version. This MUST be reported back to the sender of the unknown Code by transmitting a Code-Reject.
statements.trigger: receive LCP packet with unknown Code

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Upon reception of the Code-Reject of a code which is fundamental to this version of the protocol, the implementation SHOULD report the problem and drop the connection, since it is unlikely that the situation can be rectified automatically.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the LCP automaton is in the Opened state, then reception of a PPP packet with an unknown Protocol field MUST be reported back to the peer by transmitting a Protocol-Reject.
statements.trigger: receive packet with unknown Protocol field

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Upon reception of a Protocol-Reject, the implementation MUST stop sending packets of the indicated protocol at the earliest opportunity.
actions: stop sending packets of indicated protocol

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Protocol-Reject packets can only be sent in the LCP Opened state.
statements.guard_semantics: Protocol-Reject may only be transmitted when protocol.state = Opened

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Protocol-Reject packets received in any state other than the LCP Opened state SHOULD be silently discarded.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Upon reception of an Echo-Request in the LCP Opened state, an Echo-Reply MUST be transmitted.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Echo-Request and Echo-Reply packets received in any state other than the LCP Opened state SHOULD be silently discarded.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Echo-Request and Echo-Reply packets MUST only be sent in the LCP Opened state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Discard-Request packets MUST only be sent in the LCP Opened state.

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: On reception, the receiver MUST silently discard any Discard-Request that it receives.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: An implementation MUST NOT include multiple Authentication-Protocol Configuration Options in its Configure-Request packets.
statements.guard_semantics: cardinality=1 when Authentication-Protocol negotiation is active

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If that protocol is Configure-Nak'd, then the implementation SHOULD attempt the next most desirable protocol in the next Configure-Request.
actions: select next most desirable authentication protocol
send Configure-Request with new Authentication-Protocol option

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If an implementation sends a Configure-Ack, then it is agreeing to authenticate with the specified protocol.
actions: commit to authenticate using specified Authentication-Protocol

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An implementation receiving a Configure-Ack SHOULD expect the peer to authenticate with the acknowledged protocol.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The implementation sending the Configure-Request is indicating that it expects to receive monitoring information from its peer.
actions: indicate expectation to receive link quality monitoring data from peer

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If an implementation sends a Configure-Ack, then it is agreeing to send the specified protocol.
actions: agree to send the specified link quality monitoring protocol

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An implementation receiving a Configure-Ack SHOULD expect the peer to send the acknowledged protocol.
actions: set expectation that peer will send the acknowledged link quality monitoring protocol

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: When a Configure-Request is received with a Magic-Number Configuration Option and the two Magic-Numbers are different, then the link is not looped-back, and the Magic-Number SHOULD be acknowledged.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the two Magic-Numbers are equal, then it is possible that the link is looped-back. To determine this, a Configure-Nak MUST be sent specifying a different Magic-Number value.
actions: Send Configure-Nak with different Magic-Number value

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A new Configure-Request SHOULD NOT be sent to the peer until normal processing would cause it to be sent (that is, until a Configure-Nak is received or the Restart timer runs out).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Reception of a Configure-Nak with a Magic-Number different from that of the last Configure-Nak sent to the peer proves that a link is not looped-back, and a new Configure-Request SHOULD be sent with the new Magic-Number.
actions: Send new Configure-Request with new Magic-Number

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the Magic-Number is equal to the one sent in the last Configure-Nak, the possibility of a looped-back link is increased, and a new Magic-Number MUST be chosen. In either case, a new Configure-Request SHOULD be sent with the new Magic-Number.
actions: Send new Configure-Request with new Magic-Number

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If an implementation does receive a Configure-Reject in response to a Configure-Request, it can only mean that the link is not looped-back, and that its peer will not be using Magic-Numbers. In this case, an implementation SHOULD act as if the negotiation had been successful (as if it had instead received a Configure-Ack).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Reception of a Magic-Number field equal to the negotiated local Magic-Number indicates a looped-back link. A somewhat pessimistic procedure is to assume a LCP Down event.
statements.trigger: Reception of local Magic-Number in Echo-Request/Echo-Reply/Discard-Request

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A further Open event will begin the process of re-establishing the link, which can't complete until the looped-back condition is terminated, and Magic-Numbers are successfully negotiated.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If Magic-Number has been successfully negotiated, an implementation MUST transmit LCP Echo-Request, Echo-Reply, and Discard-Request packets with the Magic-Number field set to its negotiated Magic-Number.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If an implementation does transmit a Configure-Request with a Magic-Number Configuration Option, then it MUST NOT respond with a Configure-Reject when it receives a Configure-Request with a Magic-Number Configuration Option.
